what: KB Financial Group is one of South Korea's largest financial groups. It owns Kookmin Bank, the country's biggest retail bank by customers, plus securities, insurance and card businesses.
customers: South Korean households, small businesses and corporations, plus insurance and securities clients.
money: Kookmin Bank deposits, mortgages and corporate lending
brokerage, asset management and life and general insurance
moat: The largest retail customer base in Korea, which provides cheap deposits in a market dominated by four large groups.
risks: Korean household debt is among the highest in the world relative to income
Property project financing losses have hurt Korean banks
Regulators have intervened in bank lending and pricing
Only one analyst covers it in this data
opportunities: Net margin of 27% with a dividend yield near 3%
Korean government reforms are pushing companies to raise shareholder returns
Analysts see large upside from the current price
watch: Credit costs on property project loans and the capital return policy.
